Create an isolated Egyptian temple ruin in rolling orange desert. Make one compact rectangular sandstone temple the dominant structure, with massive decorated walls, a nearly complete flat slab roof, and an entrance facing an open forecourt. Detail the entrance with painted papyrus-style columns, square supports, low railings, and a broad shadowed opening into a dark columned interior. Keep the other three elevations mostly solid, with relief panels, hieroglyphic bands, and colored friezes. In front and slightly to one side, place a detached ruined colonnade of four tall painted columns beneath two incomplete offset lintel beams. Scatter cracked paving and fragments partly buried in sand.

graph.prompt:
Create an isolated Egyptian temple ruin in rolling orange desert. Make one compact rectangular sandstone temple the dominant structure, with massive decorated walls, a nearly complete flat slab roof, and an entrance facing an open forecourt. Detail the entrance with painted papyrus-style columns, square supports, low railings, and a broad shadowed opening into a dark columned interior. Keep the other three elevations mostly solid, with relief panels, hieroglyphic bands, and colored friezes. In front and slightly to one side, place a detached ruined colonnade of four tall painted columns beneath two incomplete offset lintel beams. Scatter cracked paving and fragments partly buried in sand.

    === GROUND ===
    Build the FLOOR FIRST, before placing anything else. Call the benchmark
    tool `ground_pass` as your first build action: it carpets the whole 200 m
    plate deterministically from a tile chosen for this scene. If you skip it,
    and do not tile a floor yourself, the scene renders as objects floating
    over empty space -- which is a failed reconstruction no matter how good
    the massing is. These palette entries are also flat surfaces you can tile
    by hand if you prefer:

      - SM_Temple_Floor | 10.0x10.0x0.50 m | /Game/EgyptianTemple/Meshes/SM_Temple_Floor.SM_Temple_Floor

You decide which to use, how many of each, and where they go — reuse entries
freely.
